<!-- thmarep-1: body_md -->
There is an isomorphism of graded algebras
\begin{gather*}
\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})\;\cong\;
\mathbb{Z}[z_1,z_3,\dots,z_{2n-1}]\otimes
\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}(\alpha_3,\alpha_7,\dots,\alpha_{4n-1}),\\
|z_{2k-1}|=4k-2,\qquad |\alpha_{4k-1}|=-(4k-1),
\end{gather*}
under which the BV operator is
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_{k=1}^{n}\ \partial_k\otimes
\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha_{4k-1}},
\qquad
\partial_k\;=\;\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2k-1}}
\;+\;2\sum_{l=k+1}^{n}z_{2(l-k)}\,
\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2l-1}} .
\]
The induced Gerstenhaber bracket is a derivation in each variable,
determined by
\[
\{z_{2l-1},\alpha_{4k-1}\}=\delta_{kl}+2z_{2(l-k)},\qquad
\{z,z'\}=\{\alpha,\alpha'\}=0 .
\]
<!-- end thmarep-1 -->
<!-- thmbrep-1: body_md -->
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair. There is an isomorphism of
BV algebras
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)\otimes R[\Gamma],
\]
with $R[\Gamma]$ the group ring of $\Gamma$, placed in degree
zero, and $\Delta_G=\Delta_{X_G}\otimes1$.
In particular $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;\mathbb{Q})\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}[\Gamma]$
for every connected compact Lie group $G$.
<!-- end thmbrep-1 -->
<!-- thmcrep-1: body_md -->
Let $R$ be an integral domain and $(G,R)$, $(G',R)$ exterior
pairs. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as BV
algebras;
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as graded $R$-algebras;
\item $G$ and $G'$ have the same exponents, and
$R[\Gamma]\cong R[\Gamma']$.
\end{enumerate}
When $\pi_1(G)$ and $\pi_1(G')$ are torsion-free, as they are
for $R=\mathbb{Z}$, condition (3) says $G\simeq_\mathbb{Q} G'$; when
$R\subseteq\mathbb{Q}$, it says $G\simeq_\mathbb{Q} G'$ and
$\pi_1(G)\cong\pi_1(G')$.
<!-- end thmcrep-1 -->
<!-- thmdrep-1: body_md -->
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair with $G$ simply connected. Then
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;HH^*\big(H^*(G;R);H^*(G;R)\big)
\]
as BV algebras, the right-hand side carrying
the cup product and the BV operator induced by Connes' operator
through Poincar\'e duality $H^*(G;R)\cong H^*(G;R)^\vee$.
<!-- end thmdrep-1 -->
<!-- conjrep-1: body_md -->
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair with $G$ simply connected. There is an
$A_\infty$ quasi-isomorphism $H^*(G;R)\to C^*(G;R)$ carrying $\Theta$
to $\theta$.
<!-- end conjrep-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:hepworth1}
For any compact Lie group $G$ there is an isomorphism of graded
algebras $\mathbb{H}_*(LG)\cong H_*(\Omega G)\otimes\mathbb{H}_*(G)$ with respect
to which the BV operator is
\[
\Delta(a\otimes x)\;=\;\sum a_{(1)}\otimes\sigma(a_{(2)})\,x .
\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:hepworth2}
Suppose either that $R$ is a field, or that $R=\mathbb{Z}$ and
$H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ is torsion-free, so that $H_*(G)$ is a Hopf
algebra. Choose a basis $p_1,\dots,p_n$ of the odd-degree part
of the primitive subspace of $H_*(G)$ and classes
$p^i\in H^*(G)$ with $\langle p^i,p_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}$.
Define
\begin{align*}
\partial_i&\colon H_*(\Omega G)\to H_{*-|p_i|+1}(\Omega G), &
\partial_i(a)&=\sum\big\langle p^i,\sigma(a_{(1)})\big\rangle\,a_{(2)},\\
\delta_i&\colon \mathbb{H}_*(G)\to\mathbb{H}_{*+|p_i|}(G), &
\delta_i(x)&=p_i\,x .
\end{align*}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:hepworth3}
In the situation of Definition~\ref{def:hepworth2} the operators
$\partial_i$ and $\delta_i$ are derivations, and under the
isomorphism of Theorem~\ref{thm:hepworth1},
$\ \Delta=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\partial_i\otimes\delta_i$.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
\label{def:exterior}
The pair $(G,R)$ is \emph{exterior} if $H_*(G;R)$ is an
exterior Hopf algebra over $R$ on finitely many primitive
generators of odd degree,
\[
H_*(G;R)\;\cong\;\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r),
\qquad
|a_k|=2m_k+1,\quad m_1\leq\dots\leq m_r.
\]
The multiset $\{m_1,\dots,m_r\}$ is the multiset of
\emph{$R$-exponents} of $G$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:whichpairs}
Let $G$ be a compact connected Lie group and $R$ a commutative
ring. Then $(G,R)$ is exterior if and only if $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has
no $p$-torsion for any prime $p$ that is not a unit in $R$,
and then the $R$-exponents are the classical exponents. In
particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(G,\mathbb{Q})$ is exterior;
\item $(G,\mathbb{Z})$ is exterior if and only if $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ is
torsion-free;
\item $(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is exterior if and only if $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has
no $p$-torsion.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Suppose $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has no $p$-torsion at the primes that are
not units in $R$. Its torsion is then a finite sum of groups
$\mathbb{Z}/q^e$ with $q$ a unit in $R$, and for these
$\mathbb{Z}/q^e\otimes R=R/q^eR=0$ and $\mathrm{Tor}(\mathbb{Z}/q^e,R)=0$, so the
universal coefficient theorem gives
$H_*(G;R)\cong(H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})/\mathrm{Tor})\otimes R$. The right-hand
side is exterior on primitive generators of the classical odd
degrees \cite[Chapter~VII, Theorem~1.22; Chapter~IV,
Theorem~2.17]{MimuraToda}, so $(G,R)$ is exterior with the
classical exponents.

Conversely let $(G,R)$ be exterior and $p$ a prime that is not
a unit in $R$. Then $p$ lies in a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$,
and $k=R/\mathfrak m$ is a field in which $p=0$, hence of
characteristic $p$. Since
$H_*(G;R)$ is free, $H_*(G;k)=H_*(G;R)\otimes_Rk$ is an
exterior algebra over $k$ on generators of odd degree, hence
so is its dual $H^*(G;k)$, and $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$
has no $p$-torsion \cite[Chapter~VII, Theorem~2.14]{MimuraToda}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:borel32}
Every connected compact Lie group is homeomorphic to the product
of its semisimple part $G_{ss}$ and the identity component of its
centre.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:borel25}
Let $G$ be a simple, simply connected compact Lie group and $p$ a
prime. Then $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has $p$-torsion exactly in the following
cases: $p=2$ and $G=\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ $(n\geq7)$, $G_2$, $F_4$,
$E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$; $p=3$ and $G=F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$;
$p=5$ and $G=E_8$.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:census}
Let $G$ be a simple simply connected compact Lie group and $R$
a commutative ring. Then $(G,R)$ is exterior if and only if
every torsion prime of $G$ is a unit in $R$, the torsion
primes being
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
group & torsion primes\\[2pt]
\hline
$\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$ & none\\
$\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ $(n\geq7)$, $G_2$ & $2$\\
$F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$ & $2,3$\\
$E_8$ & $2,3,5$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
In particular $(G,\mathbb{Q})$ is always exterior; $(G,\mathbb{Z})$ is
exterior only for $\mathrm{SU}(n)$ and $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$; and $(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is
exterior if and only if $p$ is not a torsion prime of $G$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:whichpairs}, $(G,R)$ is exterior if and
only if $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has no $p$-torsion for any prime $p$ that
is not a unit in $R$, and Theorem~\ref{thm:borel25} lists the
primes at which $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has torsion.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:pi1tors}
If $\pi_1(G)$ has torsion $\Gamma$, then
$H_1(G;\mathbb{Z})=\pi_1(G)$ has torsion, so $(G,\mathbb{Z})$ is not an
exterior pair. Over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with $p\nmid|\Gamma|$,
Proposition~\ref{prop:covering} below gives
$H_*(G_{ss};\mathbb{F}_p)\cong H_*(K;\mathbb{F}_p)$, and $(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is exterior
exactly when each simple factor of $K$ is; when
$p\mid|\Gamma|$ it can fail. For $\mathrm{SO}(3)=\mathrm{SU}(2)/(\mathbb{Z}/2)$
at $p=2$, $H^*(\mathrm{SO}(3);\mathbb{F}_2)\cong\mathbb{F}_2[x]/(x^4)$ is not
exterior, its square $x^2$ an even primitive.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:torsionfail}
The simply connected groups $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ $(n\geq7)$,
$G_2$, $F_4$, $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$ have torsion in $H_i$ for
some $i\geq2$, though $\pi_1$ is trivial; over $\mathbb{F}_p$ they are
not exterior at their torsion primes
(Theorem~\ref{thm:borel25}). For $\mathrm{Spin}(n)$ at $p=2$
the degree-three generator of $H^*(\mathrm{Spin}(n);\mathbb{F}_2)$ has
nonzero square \cite[Chapter~IV, Theorem~2.19]{MimuraToda}, an
even primitive, and so does that of each exceptional group
\cite[Chapter~VII, Section~6]{MimuraToda}; at $p=3$ and $p=5$
the exceptional groups have generators of even degree
\cite[Chapter~VII, Section~5]{MimuraToda}.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:gammaunit}
If $(G,R)$ is an exterior pair, then $|\Gamma|$ is a unit in
$R$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Let $p$ be a prime that is not a unit in $R$. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:whichpairs}, $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ has no $p$-torsion.
Since $G\cong T^k\times G_{ss}$ with $H_*(T^k;\mathbb{Z})$ free,
$H_1(G_{ss};\mathbb{Z})=\Gamma$ is a direct summand of $H_1(G;\mathbb{Z})$, so
$p\nmid|\Gamma|$. A prime dividing $|\Gamma|$ is therefore a
unit in $R$, and so is $|\Gamma|$.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:translation}
For a path-connected topological group $K$ and $g\in K$, the
translation $x\mapsto gx$ is homotopic to the identity, along
a path from $1$ to $g$. So the deck transformations of
$p\colon K\to G_{ss}$ act trivially on $H_*(K;R)$ and preserve
orientation.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:covering}
If $|\Gamma|$ is invertible in $R$, then
$p_*\colon H_*(K;R)\to H_*(G_{ss};R)$ is an isomorphism of
Hopf algebras.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Since $\Delta^n$ is simply connected, a singular simplex
$\sigma\colon\Delta^n\to G_{ss}$ has $|\Gamma|$ lifts to $K$,
one through each point of the fibre over $\sigma(e_0)$. Define
the transfer
\[
s_\#\colon C_n(G_{ss};R)\to C_n(K;R),\qquad
s_\#(\sigma)=\sum_{\tilde\sigma}\tilde\sigma,
\]
the sum over the lifts of $\sigma$. As $\tilde\sigma$ runs over
the lifts of $\sigma$, the face $\tilde\sigma\circ d_j$ runs
over the lifts of $\sigma\circ d_j$, a lift being determined by
one value; hence
\[
\partial s_\#(\sigma)
=\sum_j(-1)^j\sum_{\tilde\sigma}\tilde\sigma\circ d_j
=\sum_j(-1)^j\,s_\#(\sigma\circ d_j)
=s_\#(\partial\sigma),
\]
and $s_\#$ is a chain map. Each lift projects to $\sigma$, and
the lifts of $p\circ\tilde\sigma$ are the translates
$g\tilde\sigma$, $g\in\Gamma$, so
\[
p_\#s_\#=|\Gamma|,\qquad s_\#p_\#=\sum_{g\in\Gamma}g_\# .
\]
The translations act trivially on homology
(Lemma~\ref{lem:translation}), so $p_*s_*=|\Gamma|=s_*p_*$, and
$p_*$ is an isomorphism with inverse $|\Gamma|^{-1}s_*$, of Hopf
algebras since $p$ is a homomorphism.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:Kexterior}
If $(G,R)$ is an exterior pair, so is $(K,R)$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since $G\cong T^k\times G_{ss}$ with $H_*(T^k;\mathbb{Z})$ free,
$H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})\cong H_*(T^k;\mathbb{Z})\otimes H_*(G_{ss};\mathbb{Z})$ as graded
$\mathbb{Z}$-modules, and the two have the same torsion; so $(G_{ss},R)$ is exterior together
with $(G,R)$, the criterion of Theorem~\ref{thm:whichpairs}
being a condition on the torsion. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:gammaunit}, $|\Gamma|$ is a unit in $R$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:covering} gives
$H_*(K;R)\cong H_*(G_{ss};R)$ as Hopf algebras.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:borel}
Let $G\cong T^k\times K/\Gamma$ be a connected compact Lie group,
$K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_s$ with $K_i$ simple, and $R$ a
commutative ring. Then $(G,R)$ is an exterior pair if and only
if $|\Gamma|$ is a unit in $R$ and every $(K_i,R)$ is an
exterior pair. In particular:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $(G,\mathbb{Q})$ is an exterior pair.
\item $(G,\mathbb{Z})$ is an exterior pair if and only if $H_*(G;\mathbb{Z})$ is
torsion-free, if and only if $\Gamma=1$ and every $K_i$ is an
$\mathrm{SU}(n)$ or an $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$; $G$ is then diffeomorphic to
$T^k\times\prod_i\mathrm{SU}(n_i)\times\prod_j\mathrm{Sp}(m_j)$.
\item $(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is an exterior pair if and only if
$p\nmid|\Gamma|$ and every $(K_i,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is
(Proposition~\ref{prop:census}).
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:symbols}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair, $H_*(G;R)=\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r)$
as in Definition~\ref{def:exterior}, and $I=\{1,\dots,r\}$. For
$S\subseteq I$ let
\[
a_S:=\textstyle\prod_{i\in S}a_i,
\]
the product in increasing order of the indices, and
$a_\varnothing=1$. The set $\{a_S\}_{S\subseteq I}$ is an $R$-basis of
$H_*(G;R)$, and since the $a_i$'s are primitive,
\[
\psi(a_S)=\sum_{S=S'\sqcup S''}\pm\,a_{S'}\otimes a_{S''},
\]
with the Koszul signs of the shuffles. Let $x_S\in H^*(G;R)$ be
the dual basis under the Kronecker pairing,
$\langle x_S,a_T\rangle=\delta_{ST}$. Then
\[
H^*(G;R)=\Lambda_R(x_1,\dots,x_r),
\qquad
x_S=\textstyle\prod_{i\in S}x_i .
\]
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
\label{def:alpha}
In the situation of Definition~\ref{rem:symbols} let
$d=\dim G$, orient $G$ by $[G]:=a_I$, and let
$\mathbb{H}_*(G;R)=H_{*+d}(G;R)$ be the intersection ring,
$(x\cap[G])\cdot(y\cap[G])=(xy)\cap[G]$. For $S\subseteq I$ set
\[
\alpha_S\;:=\;x_S\cap[G]\;\in\;\mathbb{H}_{-|a_S|}(G;R),
\qquad
\alpha_i\;:=\;\alpha_{\{i\}} .
\]
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:intersection}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair. For the basis $p_i=a_i$,
Hepworth's derivations $\delta_i$ of
Definition~\ref{def:hepworth2} are the partial derivatives of
$\mathbb{H}_*(G;R)=\Lambda_R(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r)$, the derivations
of degree $|a_i|$ with
$\partial\alpha_j/\partial\alpha_i=\delta_{ij}$:
\[
\delta_i\;=\;a_i\,(-)\;=\;\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha_i}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The Pontryagin action $\delta_i$ of $a_i$ is a derivation of
degree $|a_i|$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:hepworth3}). On the
generators, $a_i\alpha_j=0$ for $j\neq i$, the factor $a_i$
repeating, and $a_i\alpha_i=[G]$ (Definition~\ref{def:alpha}).
These are the values of $\partial/\partial\alpha_i$, and two
derivations of equal degree agreeing on the generators are
equal.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:intquot}
Let $|\Gamma|$ be invertible in $R$ and $H_*(K;R)$ free, and
orient $G_{ss}$ so that $p$ preserves orientation. Then
\[
\varphi\;:=\;|\Gamma|^{-1}\,p_*\colon
\mathbb{H}_*(K;R)\longrightarrow\mathbb{H}_*(G_{ss};R)
\]
is an isomorphism of intersection rings with
$\varphi[K]=[G_{ss}]$, and
$\varphi(ax)=p_*(a)\,\varphi(x)$ for
$a\in H_*(K;R)$ and $x\in\mathbb{H}_*(K;R)$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The map $p$ is a covering of degree $|\Gamma|$ whose deck
transformations, the translations by $\Gamma$, preserve
orientation (Lemma~\ref{lem:translation}); hence
$p_*[K]=|\Gamma|\,[G_{ss}]$ and
$\varphi[K]=[G_{ss}]$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:covering},
$p_*$ is an isomorphism on homology, so $\varphi$ is
bijective, and $p^*$ is an isomorphism of cohomology rings,
the homologies being free.

Every class of $\mathbb{H}_*(K;R)$ is $p^*\xi\cap[K]$ for some
$\xi\in H^*(G_{ss};R)$. Let $x=p^*\xi\cap[K]$ and
$y=p^*\eta\cap[K]$, so that $x\cdot y=p^*(\xi\cup\eta)\cap[K]$,
the intersection product being dual to the cup product. The
projection formula gives
\[
p_*\big(p^*\zeta\cap[K]\big)=\zeta\cap p_*[K]
=|\Gamma|\,\zeta\cap[G_{ss}]
\]
for every $\zeta\in H^*(G_{ss};R)$; applied to $\xi\cup\eta$,
$\xi$ and $\eta$ it reads
$p_*(x\cdot y)=|\Gamma|^{-1}\,p_*x\cdot p_*y$, that is,
$\varphi(x\cdot y)=\varphi(x)\varphi(y)$.

The Pontryagin action is induced by the multiplication, and
$p$ is a homomorphism, so $p_*(ax)=p_*(a)\,p_*(x)$; hence
$\varphi(ax)=|\Gamma|^{-1}p_*(a)\,p_*(x)=p_*(a)\,\varphi(x)$.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:loopsplit}
For every commutative ring $R$, $\Phi$ induces an isomorphism
of Hopf algebras
\[
R[\Gamma]\otimes H_*(\Omega K;R)\;\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\;
H_*(\Omega G_{ss};R),
\]
the group ring $R[\Gamma]$ in degree zero.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:cotorext}
Let $\Lambda=\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ with the $a_i$ primitive
of odd degrees $n_i\geq3$, viewed as a coalgebra. Then, under
concatenation,
\[
H\big(\widehat\Omega\Lambda\big)\;\cong\;R[y_1,\dots,y_r],
\qquad y_i=\big[\langle a_i\rangle\big],
\]
with $y_i$ of word length one and even total degree $n_i-1$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
Every letter $\langle a_i\rangle$ is a cycle, the letters being
primitive. For $i\neq j$
\[
d\langle a_ia_j\rangle
\;=\;\pm\big(\langle a_i|a_j\rangle-\langle a_j|a_i\rangle\big).
\]
The classes $[\langle a_i\rangle]$ therefore commute, and
$y_i\mapsto[\langle a_i\rangle]$ extends to an algebra map
$R[y_1,\dots,y_r]\to H(\widehat\Omega\Lambda)$ which sends the
monomial $y_{i_1}\cdots y_{i_s}$ to the class of the word
$\langle a_{i_1}|\cdots|a_{i_s}\rangle$; it is an isomorphism
by the Koszul duality cited above.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:frame}
Let $K$ be a simply connected compact Lie group with $(K,R)$
exterior, $H_*(K;R)=\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ with the $a_k$
primitive of odd degree at least three. Then
\[
H_*(\Omega K;R)\;\cong\;R[y_1,\dots,y_r],
\qquad
|y_k|=|a_k|-1,
\]
with $y_k$ the desuspended class $\langle a_k\rangle$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{lem:cotorext} the $E_2$-page is
$R[y_1,\dots,y_r]$ as an algebra, concentrated in even total degrees and free, hence $E_2=E_\infty\cong H_*(\Omega K;R)$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:reduce}
In the situation of Definition~\ref{def:hepworth2}, let
$H_*(\Omega G;R)$ be a polynomial ring on generators
$b_1,\dots,b_r$. Then, for any basis $p_1,\dots,p_n$ of the
odd primitives of $H_*(G;R)$ and dual classes $p^i$,
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{l=1}^{r}\partial_i(b_l)\,
\frac{\partial}{\partial b_l}\otimes\delta_i.
\]
The BV operator is thus determined by the finitely many classes
$\partial_i(b_l)\in H_*(\Omega G;R)$, $1\leq i\leq n$,
$1\leq l\leq r$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:hepworth3},
$\Delta=\sum_k\partial_k\otimes\delta_k$ with each
$\partial_k$ a derivation of the polynomial ring
$H_*(\Omega G;R)$, which is
$\sum_l(\text{its value on }b_l)\,\partial/\partial b_l$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:suspzero}
For a based space $X$, $\sigma\colon H_0(\Omega X;R)\to H_1(X;R)$
sends the class of the component of $\gamma\in\pi_1(X)$ to the
Hurewicz image of $\gamma$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The evaluation map restricted to $S^1\times\{\gamma\}$ is
$\gamma$, so
$\sigma[\gamma]=\mathrm{ev}_*([S^1]\times[\gamma])=\gamma_*[S^1]$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:edge}
Let $K$ be as in Proposition~\ref{prop:frame}. Then
$\sigma(y_k)=a_k$.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
In the spectral sequence of Section~\ref{sub:frame} a class of
filtration one is represented by a word of length one, its
symbol is a desuspended primitive of $H_*(K;R)$, and the edge
map is the homology suspension
\cite[Proposition~10.25.4]{Neisendorfer}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:suspcomp}
Let $G_{ss}=K/\Gamma$ with $|\Gamma|$ invertible in $R$, and
let $r_g=\Phi(-,g)\colon\Omega K\to\Omega G_{ss}$,
$\omega\mapsto p\circ(\omega\cdot c_g)$
(Section~\ref{sub:loopspace}). Then
$\sigma_{G_{ss}}((r_g)_*1)=0$, and for
$b\in H_*(\Omega K;R)$ of positive degree
\[
\sigma_{G_{ss}}\big((r_g)_*b\big)\;=\;p_*\,\sigma_K(b),
\]
independent of $g$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
For $b=1$: $(r_g)_*1$ is the class of the component of $g$,
and its suspension is the Hurewicz image of $g$ in
$H_1(G_{ss};R)=\Gamma\otimes R$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:suspzero}),
which is zero since $|\Gamma|$ is invertible in $R$.

Let $|b|>0$. Since $p$ is a homomorphism with
$p(c_g(0))=p(c_g(1))=1$, the map $\gamma_g:=p\circ c_g$ is a
loop in $G_{ss}$ at $1$, and
\[
\mathrm{ev}\big(t,r_g(\omega)\big)=p(\omega(t))\,\gamma_g(t).
\]
So $\mathrm{ev}\circ(\mathrm{id}\times r_g)$ is the composite
\[
S^1\times\Omega K\xrightarrow{\ D\ }
(S^1\times\Omega K)\times S^1
\xrightarrow{\ (p\circ\mathrm{ev}_K)\times\gamma_g\ }
G_{ss}\times G_{ss}\xrightarrow{\ \mu\ }G_{ss},
\qquad D(t,\omega)=((t,\omega),t),
\]
with $\mathrm{ev}_K$ the evaluation of $K$ and $\mu$ the
multiplication. The diagonal of $S^1$ sends $[S^1]$ to
$[S^1]\times[\mathrm{pt}]+[\mathrm{pt}]\times[S^1]$, so
\[
D_*\big([S^1]\times b\big)
=\big([S^1]\times b\big)\times[\mathrm{pt}]
+(-1)^{|b|}\big([\mathrm{pt}]\times b\big)\times[S^1].
\]
The second term dies under $\mathrm{ev}_K$: $\mathrm{ev}_K(0,\omega)=\omega(0)=1$
is constant and $|b|>0$. The first is carried to
$p_*\sigma_K(b)\times[1]$, since
$\mathrm{ev}_{K*}([S^1]\times b)=\sigma_K(b)$ and
$\gamma_{g*}[\mathrm{pt}]=[1]$, and then to
$p_*\sigma_K(b)$ by $\mu$, as $[1]$ is the unit. Hence
$\sigma_{G_{ss}}((r_g)_*b)=\mathrm{ev}_*([S^1]\times(r_g)_*b)
=p_*\sigma_K(b)$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:sigmaprops}
Let $X$ be a based space and $e,e'\in H_*(\Omega X;R)$ of
positive degree. Then $\sigma(ee')=0$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $a\colon\Omega X\times PX\to PX$, $a(\omega,\gamma)=\omega*\gamma$,
concatenate a loop in front of a path. It carries
$\Omega X\times\Omega X$ into $\Omega X$, where it is the
concatenation inducing the Pontryagin product, and it
preserves endpoints: $q\circ a=q\circ\mathrm{pr}_2$ for the
projection $\mathrm{pr}_2\colon\Omega X\times PX\to PX$. So
$a$ is a map of pairs
$(\Omega X\times PX,\Omega X\times\Omega X)\to(PX,\Omega X)$.

Let $u$ be the class with $\partial u=e'$. The cross product
$e\times u\in H_*(\Omega X\times PX,\Omega X\times\Omega X)$
has $\partial(e\times u)=(-1)^{|e|}e\times e'$, $e$ being an
absolute class, so
$\partial\,a_*(e\times u)=(-1)^{|e|}a_*(e\times e')=(-1)^{|e|}ee'$.
By the description of $\sigma$ above,
$\sigma(ee')=(-1)^{|e|}\,q_*a_*(e\times u)$.

Now $q_*a_*=q_*\mathrm{pr}_{2*}$, and $\mathrm{pr}_2$ collapses
the first factor to a point, so
$\mathrm{pr}_{2*}(e\times u)=\varepsilon(e)\,u$. Since $|e|>0$,
$\varepsilon(e)=0$, and hence $\sigma(ee')=0$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:indec}
Let $(K,R)$ be an exterior pair with $K$ simply connected,
$H_*(K;R)=\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r)$, and the exponents of $K$
pairwise distinct. Then for any polynomial generators
$b_1,\dots,b_r$ of $H_*(\Omega K;R)$, after reindexing,
$\sigma(b_k)=u_k\,a_k$ with $u_k\in R^\times$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:frame} and Lemma~\ref{lem:edge},
$H_*(\Omega K;R)=R[y_1,\dots,y_r]$ with $\sigma(y_k)=a_k$. The
degrees are distinct, so after reindexing $|b_k|=|y_k|$ and
$b_k=u_ky_k+{}$decomposable, with $u_k$ a unit since the $b_k$
generate. The suspension $\sigma$ kills decomposables (Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaprops}),
so $\sigma(b_k)=u_ka_k$.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
\label{thm:kk}
The Pontryagin ring
$H_*(\Omega\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}[z_1,z_3,\dots,z_{2n-1}]$ is a
polynomial ring on generators $z_{2k-1}$ of degree $4k-2$, with
coproduct
\[
\psi(z_r)\;=\;z_r\otimes1+1\otimes z_r
+2\!\!\sum_{\substack{i+j=r\\ i,j\geq1}}\!\!z_i\otimes z_j
\qquad(r\ \text{odd}),
\]
where the classes of even index are the universal integral
polynomials in the odd generators given by the recursion
\[
z_{2m}\;=\;2\sum_{i=1}^{m-1}(-1)^{i+1}z_i\,z_{2m-i}
+(-1)^{m+1}z_m^{2},
\]
with the convention $z_{2m}=0$ for $m\leq0$.
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:susp}
The classes $\sigma(z_1),\sigma(z_3),\dots,\sigma(z_{2n-1})$
are a basis of the odd primitives of $H_*(\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$, and
$\sigma(z_{2j})=0$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
The exponents of $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$ are distinct, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:indec} applies to the polynomial generators
$z_{2k-1}$. Every term of the recursion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:kk} is a product of two classes of positive
degree, so $z_{2j}$ is decomposable and $\sigma(z_{2j})=0$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:sigmaprops}).
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:partial}
With respect to the presentation of Theorem~\ref{thm:kk}, the
derivations $\partial_k$ of Definition~\ref{def:hepworth2} for
the basis $p_k=a_{4k-1}$ are
\[
\partial_k\;=\;\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2k-1}}
\;+\;2\sum_{l=k+1}^{n}z_{2(l-k)}\,
\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2l-1}},
\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
\partial_k(z_{2l-1})=\delta_{kl}+2\,z_{2(l-k)},
\]
with $z_{2m}=0$ for $m\leq0$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
By Proposition~\ref{prop:reduce}, $\partial_k$ is the
derivation with
$\partial_k(z_{2l-1})=\sum\langle x_{4k-1},\sigma(z_{2l-1,(1)})\rangle\,z_{2l-1,(2)}$.
The coproduct of Theorem~\ref{thm:kk} has the terms
$z_{2l-1}\otimes1$, $1\otimes z_{2l-1}$, and $2z_i\otimes z_j$
with $i+j=2l-1$ and $i,j\geq1$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:susp},
$\langle x_{4k-1},\sigma(z_i)\rangle=\delta_{i,2k-1}$ for
$i\geq1$, and $\sigma(1)=0$. The three kinds of terms therefore
contribute $\delta_{kl}$, $0$, and $2z_{2l-1-(2k-1)}=2z_{2(l-k)}$,
the last only when $l>k$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{thmA}
There is an isomorphism of graded algebras
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})\;\cong\;
\mathbb{Z}[z_1,z_3,\dots,z_{2n-1}]\otimes
\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}(\alpha_3,\alpha_7,\dots,\alpha_{4n-1}),
\]
with $|z_{2k-1}|=4k-2$ and $|\alpha_{4k-1}|=-(4k-1)$, under which
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_{k=1}^{n}\ \partial_k\otimes
\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha_{4k-1}},
\qquad
\partial_k\;=\;\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2k-1}}
\;+\;2\sum_{l=k+1}^{n}z_{2(l-k)}\,
\frac{\partial}{\partial z_{2l-1}}\,,
\]
and the induced Gerstenhaber bracket of degree $1$ is
determined by
\[
\{z_{2l-1},\alpha_{4k-1}\}\;=\;\delta_{kl}+2\,z_{2(l-k)},
\qquad
\{z,z'\}\;=\;\{\alpha,\alpha'\}\;=\;0 ,
\]
the bracket being a derivation in each variable.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:hepworth1},
$\mathbb{H}_*(L\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})\cong H_*(\Omega\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})\otimes\mathbb{H}_*(\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$
as graded algebras, which is the polynomial ring of
Theorem~\ref{thm:kk} tensored with the exterior ring above.

The homology $H_*(\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ is torsion-free, so
Proposition~\ref{prop:hepworth3} applies over $\mathbb{Z}$:
$\Delta=\sum_k\partial_k\otimes\delta_k$ for the basis
$p_k=a_{4k-1}$, with $\delta_k=\partial/\partial\alpha_{4k-1}$
as above and $\partial_k$ as in Proposition~\ref{prop:partial}.

For the bracket, in the convention
$\Delta(ab)=\Delta(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\Delta(b)+(-1)^{|a|}\{a,b\}$,
$\Delta$ vanishes on $\mathbb{Z}[z]\otimes1$, which carries no
$\alpha$, and on the $\alpha_{4k-1}$, as $\partial_k(1)=0$.
Hence
\[
\{z_{2l-1},\alpha_{4k-1}\}
=\Delta\big(z_{2l-1}\alpha_{4k-1}\big)
=\partial_k(z_{2l-1})
=\delta_{kl}+2\,z_{2(l-k)},
\]
and likewise $\{z,z'\}=\Delta(zz')=0$ and
$\{\alpha,\alpha'\}=\Delta(\alpha\alpha')=0$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:degen}
The primitives of $H_{4k-2}(\Omega\mathrm{Sp}(n);\mathbb{Z})$ form a free
module of rank one, on a class
$\rho_k\equiv(2k-1)\,z_{2k-1}$ modulo decomposables
\cite[\S5]{KonoKozima}. Once the integers $1,3,\dots,2n-1$ are
inverted, over $\mathbb{Z}[1/(2n-1)!]$ or $p$-locally for $p>2n-1$, the
classes $(2k-1)^{-1}\rho_k$ are polynomial generators, they are
primitive, and $\Delta$ is a pure tensor
(Definition~\ref{def:mixing}). The next section shows that no
localization is needed.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:product}
Let $M$, $N$ be closed oriented manifolds with $H_*(LM;R)$ a
free $R$-module. Then the K\"unneth map is an isomorphism of
Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LM;R)\otimes\mathbb{H}_*(LN;R)\;\cong\;\mathbb{H}_*(L(M\times N);R),
\qquad
\Delta_{M\times N}\;=\;\Delta_M\otimes1+1\otimes\Delta_N .
\]
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Since $L(M\times N)=LM\times LN$ and $H_*(LM;R)$ is free, the
K\"unneth map is an isomorphism of graded modules.

It is multiplicative. Let $m=\dim M$ and $n=\dim N$. The loop
product of $M$ is the composite
\[
H_*(LM\times LM)\xrightarrow{\ \tau\ }H_{*-m}(LM\times_MLM)
\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{concat}_*\ }H_{*-m}(LM),
\]
where $LM\times_MLM=\mathrm{ev}^{-1}(\Delta_M)$ is the space of
composable pairs, for
$\mathrm{ev}\colon LM\times LM\to M\times M$,
$(\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(\alpha(0),\beta(0))$, and
$\tau=(-)\cap u_M$ is the Thom collapse: $\mathrm{ev}$ is a
fibration, so a tubular neighbourhood of $\Delta_M$ pulls back
to one of $LM\times_MLM$, the total space of
$\mathrm{ev}^*\nu_M$ for the normal bundle $\nu_M$ of the
diagonal, and $u_M$ is the pullback of its Thom class.

A loop in $M\times N$ is a pair of loops, $L(M\times N)=LM\times LN$.
Swapping the middle factors of $(LM\times LN)\times(LM\times LN)$
identifies it with $(LM\times LM)\times(LN\times LN)$,
$\mathrm{ev}_{M\times N}$ with $\mathrm{ev}_M\times\mathrm{ev}_N$
and $\Delta_{M\times N}$ with $\Delta_M\times\Delta_N$. Hence the
composable pairs of $M\times N$ are
$(LM\times_MLM)\times(LN\times_NLN)$; the normal bundle of
$\Delta_M\times\Delta_N$ is $\nu_M\times\nu_N$, with Thom class
$u_M\times u_N$; and concatenation in $M\times N$ is
componentwise, $\mathrm{concat}_M\times\mathrm{concat}_N$. For
$a,a'\in H_*(LM)$ and $b,b'\in H_*(LN)$,
\begin{align*}
(a\times b)\cdot(a'\times b')
&=\mathrm{concat}_*\big((a\times b\times a'\times b')\cap u_{M\times N}\big)\\
&=\pm\,(\mathrm{concat}_M\times\mathrm{concat}_N)_*
\big(((a\times a')\cap u_M)\times((b\times b')\cap u_N)\big)\\
&=\pm\,(a\cdot a')\times(b\cdot b'),
\end{align*}
the signs Koszul signs, from the swap and from the cap product
of cross products. So the K\"unneth map is multiplicative for
the tensor product of graded algebras.

For the BV operators, $\Delta_M(a)=\rho_{M*}([S^1]\times a)$ for the
rotation $\rho_M\colon S^1\times LM\to LM$. The rotation of
$M\times N$ is $(t,\alpha,\beta)\mapsto(\rho_M(t,\alpha),\rho_N(t,\beta))$,
which factors through the diagonal $D$ of $S^1$, and
$D_*[S^1]=[S^1]\times1+1\times[S^1]$; so
\[
\Delta_{M\times N}(a\times b)
=\Delta_M(a)\times b+(-1)^{|a|}a\times\Delta_N(b),
\]
that is, $\Delta_{M\times N}=\Delta_M\otimes1+1\otimes\Delta_N$.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:spheres}
For $X=S^{2m_1+1}\times\cdots\times S^{2m_r+1}$ with $m_k\geq1$,
\begin{gather*}
\mathbb{H}_*(LX;\mathbb{Z})\;\cong\;\mathbb{Z}[u_{2m_1},\dots,u_{2m_r}]\otimes
\Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}}(d_{2m_1+1},\dots,d_{2m_r+1}),\\
\Delta_X\;=\;\sum_{k=1}^{r}
\frac{\partial}{\partial u_{2m_k}}\otimes
\frac{\partial}{\partial d_{2m_k+1}}.
\end{gather*}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
For one odd sphere,
$\mathbb{H}_*(LS^{2m+1};\mathbb{Z})\cong\mathbb{Z}[u_{2m}]\otimes\Lambda_\mathbb{Z}(d_{2m+1})$
with $\Delta=\partial/\partial u_{2m}\otimes\partial/\partial d_{2m+1}$
\cite[Theorem~16]{Menichi}. Lemma~\ref{lem:product}, applied
factor by factor, gives the tensor product of these algebras
with $\Delta_X=\sum_k\mathrm{id}\otimes\cdots\otimes\Delta_k\otimes
\cdots\otimes\mathrm{id}$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\label{def:mixing}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair and let $H_*(\Omega G;R)$ be a
polynomial ring on generators $b_1,\dots,b_r$ whose homology
suspensions $p_k=\sigma(b_k)$ are a basis of the odd primitives
of $H_*(G;R)$. Let $\partial_k$, $\delta_k$ be the operators of
Definition~\ref{def:hepworth2} for this basis. The
\emph{mixing terms} of the presentation $\{b_k\}$ are the
classes
\[
\gamma_{kl}\;:=\;\partial_k(b_l)-\delta_{kl}
\;\in\;H_*(\Omega G;R),
\]
so that
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_{k}\frac{\partial}{\partial b_k}\otimes\delta_k
\;+\;\sum_{k,l}\gamma_{kl}\,
\frac{\partial}{\partial b_l}\otimes\delta_k
\]
by Proposition~\ref{prop:reduce}. The presentation is
\emph{unmixed} if every $\gamma_{kl}$ vanishes, that is, if
$\Delta$ is a pure tensor.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{thm:shear}
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let
\[
\mathbb{H}\;=\;R[b_1,\dots,b_r]\otimes\Lambda_R(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r),
\]
with the $b_k$ of positive even degree and the $\alpha_k$ of
odd degree, be a Batalin-Vilkovisky algebra whose BV operator has
the form
\[
\Delta\;=\;\sum_{k=1}^{r}\partial_k\otimes
\frac{\partial}{\partial\alpha_k},
\qquad
\partial_k(b_l)\;=\;\delta_{kl}+\gamma_{kl},
\]
with each $\partial_k$ a derivation of the polynomial factor and
each $\gamma_{kl}$ a polynomial of degree $|b_l|-|b_k|$, zero
unless $|b_l|>|b_k|$. Then
\[
\Phi(b_k)\;=\;u_k,
\qquad
\Phi(\alpha_k)\;=\;d_k+\sum_{l}\gamma_{kl}(u)\,d_l,
\]
with $\gamma_{kl}(u)$ the polynomial $\gamma_{kl}$ evaluated at
$b_i=u_i$, defines an isomorphism of Batalin-Vilkovisky
algebras onto the pure tensor
\[
R[u_1,\dots,u_r]\otimes\Lambda_R(d_1,\dots,d_r),
\qquad
\Delta_X\;=\;\sum_{k=1}^{r}\frac{\partial}{\partial u_k}\otimes
\frac{\partial}{\partial d_k},
\]
with $|u_k|=|b_k|$ and $|d_k|=|\alpha_k|$.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
Write $c_{km}=\delta_{km}+\gamma_{km}(u)$, so
$\Phi(\alpha_k)=\sum_m c_{km}d_m$; the $c_{km}$ are even.

The source is free graded-commutative on the even $b_k$ and
the odd $\alpha_k$, and the $\Phi(\alpha_k)$ are odd with even
coefficients, so $\Phi$ is a ring map. It is the identity on
$R[u]$ and, on the $R[u]$-module spanned by the $d_m$, the
matrix $(c_{km})$, unitriangular for the generators ordered by
degree since $\gamma_{km}=0$ unless $|b_m|>|b_k|$. So $\Phi$ is
a ring isomorphism.

The operator $\Delta_X$ is a BV operator. Each summand
$\partial/\partial u_k\otimes\partial/\partial d_k$ is the
composite of two commuting derivations, hence a differential
operator of order at most two, and so is the sum; and
\[
\Delta_X^2=\sum_{k,l}\frac{\partial^2}{\partial u_k\,\partial u_l}
\otimes\frac{\partial^2}{\partial d_k\,\partial d_l}=0,
\]
the first factor being symmetric in $k,l$ and the second
antisymmetric. Conjugation by the ring isomorphism $\Phi$
preserves both properties, so $\Delta':=\Phi^{-1}\Delta_X\Phi$
is a BV operator. The seven-term relation
is linear in the BV operator and expresses the value on a product
of three or more generators through values on shorter
products, so $\Delta'=\Delta$ once the two agree on $1$, on
the generators and on the products of two generators:
on $1$, $b_k$, $\alpha_k$, $b_lb_m$, $b_l\alpha_k$ and
$\alpha_k\alpha_j$.

On the target, for a polynomial $P$ in the $u$'s,
\[
\Delta_X(P\,d_m)=\frac{\partial P}{\partial u_m},
\qquad
\Delta_X(P\,d_md_n)=\frac{\partial P}{\partial u_m}\,d_n
-\frac{\partial P}{\partial u_n}\,d_m,
\]
and $\Delta_X$ vanishes on $R[u]$. On the source, $\Delta$
vanishes on $R[b]$, and $\Delta(\alpha_k)=\partial_k(1)=0$,
$\Delta(b_l\alpha_k)=\partial_k(b_l)$,
$\Delta(\alpha_k\alpha_j)=0$. The polynomial $\gamma_{km}$ has
degree $|b_m|-|b_k|<|b_m|$, so it does not involve $u_m$, and
$\sum_m\partial c_{km}/\partial u_m=0$.

Both BV operators vanish on $1$, $b_k$ and $b_lb_m$. On $\alpha_k$
and $b_l\alpha_k$,
\[
\Delta_X\Phi(\alpha_k)=\sum_m\frac{\partial c_{km}}{\partial u_m}=0,
\qquad
\Delta_X\Phi(b_l\alpha_k)
=\sum_m\frac{\partial(u_lc_{km})}{\partial u_m}
=c_{kl}=\Phi\big(\partial_k(b_l)\big).
\]

For $\alpha_k\alpha_j$, applying $\Delta$ twice to
$b_n\alpha_k\alpha_j$ gives $[\partial_j,\partial_k](b_n)$, so
$\Delta^2=0$ says the $\partial_k$ commute:
$\partial_k(\gamma_{jn})=\partial_j(\gamma_{kn})$. In the
$u$'s, $\partial_k=\sum_mc_{km}\,\partial/\partial u_m$, and
\begin{align*}
\Delta_X\big(\Phi(\alpha_k)\Phi(\alpha_j)\big)
&=\sum_{m,n}\frac{\partial(c_{km}c_{jn})}{\partial u_m}\,d_n
-\sum_{m,n}\frac{\partial(c_{km}c_{jn})}{\partial u_n}\,d_m\\
&=\sum_n\big(\partial_k(\gamma_{jn})-\partial_j(\gamma_{kn})\big)(u)\,d_n
\;=\;0,
\end{align*}
the sums $\sum_m\partial c_{km}/\partial u_m$ and
$\sum_n\partial c_{jn}/\partial u_n$ vanishing. So
$\Delta'=\Delta$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{thm:rigid}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair with $\pi_1(G)$ torsion-free,
that is, with $G_{ss}$ simply connected. Then there is an
isomorphism of Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R).
\]
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:borel32}, $G\cong T^k\times K$ with $K=G_{ss}$
simply connected and $(K,R)$ exterior
(Corollary~\ref{cor:Kexterior}), and $X_G=T^k\times X_K$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:product} both sides have $\mathbb{H}_*(LT^k;R)$ tensored
with the $K$-side, with the same BV operator on the torus factor,
so it suffices to treat $K$.

Let $H_*(K;R)=\Lambda_R(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ with $|a_k|=2m_k+1$,
$m_k\geq1$. Then $H_*(\Omega K;R)=R[y_1,\dots,y_r]$ with
$|y_k|=2m_k$ and $\sigma(y_k)=a_k$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:frame},
Lemma~\ref{lem:edge}), $\mathbb{H}_*(K;R)=\Lambda_R(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r)$
with $\delta_k=\partial/\partial\alpha_k$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:intersection}), and
$\Delta_K=\sum_k\partial_k\otimes\partial/\partial\alpha_k$
(Proposition~\ref{prop:reduce}). The mixing terms are
triangular (Section~\ref{sub:mixing}), so
Proposition~\ref{thm:shear} applies, and
its target, with $|u_k|=2m_k$ and $|d_k|=-(2m_k+1)$, is
$\mathbb{H}_*(LX_K;R)$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:spheres}).
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{cor:classify}
Let $R$ be an integral domain and $(G,R)$, $(G',R)$ exterior
pairs with $\pi_1(G)$ and $\pi_1(G')$ torsion-free. The
following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as Batalin-Vilkovisky
algebras;
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as graded algebras;
\item $G$ and $G'$ have the same multiset of $R$-exponents;
\item $G$ and $G'$ are rationally homotopy equivalent.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
(3)$\Rightarrow$(1): both algebras are BV-isomorphic to
$\mathbb{H}_*(LX;R)$ for the common $X=X_G=X_{G'}$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}). (1)$\Rightarrow$(2) is trivial.

(2)$\Rightarrow$(3). It is enough to recover the exponents of
$G$ from the graded algebra $A=\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$. Let $k$ be the
multiplicity of the exponent $0$ and $\{m_1,\dots,m_r\}$ the
positive exponents. By Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid},
Lemma~\ref{lem:product} and Proposition~\ref{prop:spheres},
\[
A\;\cong\;R[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]\otimes
\Lambda_R(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_k)\otimes
R[b_1,\dots,b_r]\otimes\Lambda_R(\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r),
\]
the first two factors being $\mathbb{H}_*(LT^k;R)$, with
\[
|t_i|=0,\qquad|\theta_i|=-1,\qquad
|b_j|=2m_j,\qquad|\alpha_j|=-(2m_j+1).
\]
The odd generators $\theta_i$, $\alpha_j$ anticommute and
square to zero, so the ideal $N$ they generate is nilpotent.
The quotient $A/N=R[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}][b_1,\dots,b_r]$
is an integral domain, $R$ being one. Hence $N$ is the
nilradical of $A$, and $\bar A:=A/N$ depends only on the ring
$A$. The degree-zero part of $\bar A$ is the
Laurent polynomial ring $R[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$, whose
base change to the fraction field $F$ of $R$ is
$F[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$, of Krull dimension $k$; this
gives $k$. In positive degrees
$\bar A$ is a polynomial ring over its degree-zero part, whose
indecomposables are free with basis in degrees
$2m_1,\dots,2m_r$; this gives the positive exponents.

(3)$\Leftrightarrow$(4): the $R$-exponents are the classical
exponents (Theorem~\ref{thm:whichpairs}), and the map
$X_G\to G$ of Section~\ref{sub:exterior} is a rational
homotopy equivalence, so the exponents and the rational
homotopy type determine one another.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:sharp}
Let $(K,\mathbb{Z})$ be an exterior pair with $K$ simply connected,
and $f$ a based map between $X_K$ and $K$, in either direction,
with $Lf_*$ an isomorphism on integral homology. The constant
loops $c$ split the evaluation, $\mathrm{ev}\circ c=\mathrm{id}$,
and $Lf\circ c=c\circ f$, $\mathrm{ev}\circ Lf=f\circ\mathrm{ev}$;
so $f_*$ is a retract of $Lf_*$, hence an isomorphism, and $f$
is a homotopy equivalence of simply connected finite complexes.
Then $\Omega f$ is an equivalence of $H$-spaces and
$H_*(\Omega X_K)\cong H_*(\Omega K)$ as Hopf algebras. But
$H_*(\Omega X_K)$ is primitively generated and $H_*(\Omega K)$
is not for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, whose primitive in degree $6$ is
$3z_3-2z_1^3$ (Remark~\ref{rem:degen}), nor for $\mathrm{SU}(n)$,
$n\geq3$, whose primitive in degree $4$ is $2e_4-e_2^2$
\cite[Theorem~2-1]{Tamanoi}; and already $\pi_6(S^3\times S^7)$
and $\pi_6(S^3\times S^5)$ contain $\pi_6(S^3)$, of order $12$
\cite[Proposition~10]{Serre53}, while $\pi_6(\mathrm{Sp}(2))=0$ and
$\pi_6(\mathrm{SU}(3))$ has order $6$
\cite[Theorems~5.1 and~4.1]{MimuraToda2}. For these groups the
isomorphism of Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid} is not induced by a map
of spaces.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:rational}
Over $\mathbb{Q}$ the isomorphism of Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid} is forced
by formality. Write $G\cong T^k\times K$ with $K$ simply
connected. Both $K$ and $X_K$ are rationally formal, their
cohomology being exterior on odd generators, and F\'elix and
Thomas build the rational BV algebra of the free loop space of
a simply connected closed manifold from a Poincar\'e duality
model of its cochains
\cite[Theorem~1, Propositions~1 and~2]{FelixThomas}; the common
cohomology of $K$ and $X_K$, with its pairing, is such a model
for both.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
\label{thm:hochmodel}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair with $G$ simply connected. Then
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;HH^*\big(H^*(G;R);H^*(G;R)\big)
\]
as Batalin-Vilkovisky algebras, the right-hand side carrying the
cup product and the BV operator induced by Connes' operator through
Poincar\'e duality $H^*(G;R)\cong H^*(G;R)^\vee$.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid}, $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)$ as
BV algebras, and $H^*(G;R)\cong H^*(X_G;R)$ as graded algebras;
an algebra isomorphism changes $\Theta$ by a unit, which
cancels in $\Theta_*^{-1}B^\vee\Theta_*$. So it suffices to
treat $X_G$.

For one sphere, $A=\Lambda_R(x)$ with $|x|=n$ odd, Menichi
computes $HH^*(A;A)$ with its BV operator over $\mathbb{F}_2$
\cite[Proposition~20]{Menichi} from Connes' operator on the
Hochschild chains \cite[Example~12]{Menichi}; the example is
stated over any commutative ring, and for $n$ odd its signs make
the differential vanish and the BV operator integral, so
\[
HH^*(A;A)=\Lambda_R(g)\otimes R[f],\qquad
\Delta(gf^k)=k\,f^{k-1},\qquad \Delta(f^k)=0 ,
\]
which is $\mathbb{H}_*(LS^n;R)$ \cite[Theorem~16]{Menichi}.

For products, the K\"unneth map
$HH^*(A;A)\otimes HH^*(B;B)\to HH^*(A\otimes B;A\otimes B)$ of
symmetric algebras is a map of BV algebras, an isomorphism when
one factor has projective Hochschild cohomology
\cite[Theorems~3.5 and~3.8, Corollary~3.9]{DuarteAngel}. Their
algebras are ungraded and their ring hereditary, but the
argument applies with Koszul signs to $\Lambda_R(x)$ over any
$R$, the cochains having zero differential and free cohomology.
With Lemma~\ref{lem:product} on the loop side,
$\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)\cong HH^*\big(H^*(X_G;R);H^*(X_G;R)\big)$ as BV
algebras.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- conjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{conj:pdformal}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair with $G$ simply connected,
$\Theta$ the Poincar\'e duality isomorphism of $H^*(G;R)$ and
$\theta$ the class of the constant loops for $C^*(G;R)$. There
is an $A_\infty$ quasi-isomorphism
$f\colon H^*(G;R)\to C^*(G;R)$ carrying $\Theta$ to $\theta$.
<!-- end conjecture-1 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
\label{thm:torsionss}
Let $K$ be a compact simply connected Lie group with $(K,R)$
exterior, $\Gamma\subset K$ a finite central subgroup with
$|\Gamma|$ a unit in $R$, and $G_{ss}=K/\Gamma$. Then
\[
\Xi:=\Phi_*\otimes\varphi\colon
\mathbb{H}_*(LK;R)\otimes R[\Gamma]\;\longrightarrow\;
\mathbb{H}_*(LG_{ss};R),
\qquad
(b\otimes x)\otimes g\;\longmapsto\;(r_g)_*b\otimes\varphi(x),
\]
is an isomorphism of BV algebras, with $R[\Gamma]$ in degree zero
and zero BV operator.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{thm:hepworth1} for $K$ and for $G_{ss}$,
$\Xi$ is $\Phi_*$ on the Pontryagin factor and $\varphi$ on
the intersection factor, both ring isomorphisms
(Proposition~\ref{prop:loopsplit}, Lemma~\ref{lem:intquot}),
and $R[\Gamma]$ is in degree zero. So $\Xi$ is a ring
isomorphism.

For the BV operators let $b\in H_*(\Omega K;R)$ with
$\psi(b)=\sum b_{(1)}\otimes b_{(2)}$. The isomorphism $\Phi_*$ is
a map of coalgebras and $g$ is group-like, so
$\psi((r_g)_*b)=\sum(r_g)_*b_{(1)}\otimes(r_g)_*b_{(2)}$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:hepworth1} for $G_{ss}$ gives
\[
\Delta_{G_{ss}}\Xi\big((b\otimes x)\otimes g\big)
=\sum(r_g)_*b_{(1)}\otimes
\sigma_{G_{ss}}\big((r_g)_*b_{(2)}\big)\,\varphi(x).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:suspcomp},
$\sigma_{G_{ss}}((r_g)_*b_{(2)})$ is $0$ for $b_{(2)}=1$ and
$p_*\sigma_K(b_{(2)})$ otherwise, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:intquot},
$p_*\sigma_K(b_{(2)})\,\varphi(x)=\varphi(\sigma_K(b_{(2)})\,x)$.
Hence
\[
\Delta_{G_{ss}}\Xi\big((b\otimes x)\otimes g\big)
=\sum(r_g)_*b_{(1)}\otimes\varphi\big(\sigma_K(b_{(2)})\,x\big)
=\Xi\big(\Delta_K(b\otimes x)\otimes g\big),
\]
the last equality being Theorem~\ref{thm:hepworth1} for $K$,
with $\sigma_K(1)=0$.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
\label{thmE}
Let $(G,R)$ be an exterior pair and $\Gamma$ the torsion
subgroup of $\pi_1(G)$. Then there is an isomorphism of BV
algebras
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)\otimes R[\Gamma],
\]
with $R[\Gamma]$ the group ring of $\Gamma$, placed in degree
zero with zero BV operator, so that
$\Delta_G=\Delta_{X_G}\otimes1$. In particular
$\mathbb{H}_*(LG;\mathbb{Q})\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;\mathbb{Q})\otimes\mathbb{Q}[\Gamma]$ for every
connected compact Lie group $G$.
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
The exponents of $G$ are those of $K$ together with $k$
zeros, so $X_G=T^k\times X_K$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:product},
Theorem~\ref{thm:torsionss} and Theorem~\ref{thm:rigid} for
$(K,R)$,
\begin{align*}
\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)
&\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LT^k;R)\otimes\mathbb{H}_*(LK;R)\otimes R[\Gamma]\\
&\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LT^k;R)\otimes\mathbb{H}_*(LX_K;R)\otimes R[\Gamma]
\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)\otimes R[\Gamma]
\end{align*}
as BV algebras. Over $\mathbb{Q}$ every
pair is exterior (Theorem~\ref{thm:whichpairs}).
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:torsionclass}
Let $R$ be an integral domain and $(G,R)$, $(G',R)$ exterior
pairs with torsion $\Gamma$, $\Gamma'$. The following are
equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as BV algebras;
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as graded $R$-algebras;
\item $G$ and $G'$ have the same $R$-exponents, and
$R[\Gamma]\cong R[\Gamma']$ as $R$-algebras.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
(3)$\Rightarrow$(1) is Theorem~\ref{thmE}, and
(1)$\Rightarrow$(2) is trivial. For (2)$\Rightarrow$(3), let
$k$ be the multiplicity of the exponent $0$ among the $r$
exponents of $G$ and $B=R[\Gamma][t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$.
By Theorem~\ref{thmE} and Proposition~\ref{prop:spheres},
\[
A:=\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\;\cong\;B[u_{k+1},\dots,u_r]\otimes
\Lambda_R(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_k,d_{k+1},\dots,d_r)
\]
as graded algebras, $|u_j|=2m_j$. Let $F$ be the fraction field
of $R$. As $|\Gamma|$ is a unit in $F$, $F[\Gamma]\cong\prod_iL_i$
with $L_i$ finite field extensions of $F$, so
$B\otimes_RF\cong\prod_iL_i[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$ is
reduced of Krull dimension $k$, and $B\subset B\otimes_RF$ is
reduced. Hence the odd generators span the nilradical $N$ of
$A$, and $A/N=B[u_{k+1},\dots,u_r]$. An isomorphism of graded
$R$-algebras $A\cong A'$ therefore induces isomorphisms of the
degree-zero parts $B\cong B'$ of the reduced rings, of
$B\otimes_RF$, and of the indecomposables of $A/N$ over $B$,
free on the $u_j$. This gives $k$ as the Krull dimension of
$B\otimes_RF$, the positive exponents as the degrees of the
$u_j$, and $R[\Gamma]$ as the integral closure of $R$ in $B$:
$R[\Gamma]$ is finite over $R$, and an element of $B$ integral
over $R$ is algebraic over $F$ in $\prod_iL_i[t^{\pm1}]$, hence
constant, hence in $B\cap F[\Gamma]=R[\Gamma]$.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a domain and $\Gamma\neq1$. Then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ and
$\mathbb{H}_*(LX_G;R)$ are not isomorphic even as rings. The
degree-zero parts of their reduced rings are
$R[\Gamma][t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$ and
$R[t_1^{\pm1},\dots,t_k^{\pm1}]$, and the first has zero
divisors: $(g-1)(1+g+\dots+g^{n-1})=0$ for $g$ of order $n>1$.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- corollary-5: body_md -->
\label{cor:rationalpi1}
Let $R$ be a subring of $\mathbb{Q}$, for instance $\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbb{Z}[1/n]$ or
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$, and $(G,R)$, $(G',R)$ exterior pairs. The following
are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as BV algebras;
\item $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)\cong\mathbb{H}_*(LG';R)$ as graded algebras;
\item $G$ and $G'$ have the same $R$-exponents and
$\pi_1(G)\cong\pi_1(G')$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular this holds over $\mathbb{Q}$ for all connected compact
Lie groups $G$, $G'$.
<!-- end corollary-5 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
The BV algebra sees $\pi_1(G)$ only through $R[\pi_1(G)]$, and
over $\mathbb{F}_p$ that is less than the group: for $p\equiv1\bmod4$,
$\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}/4]\cong\mathbb{F}_p^4\cong\mathbb{F}_p[\mathbb{Z}/2\times\mathbb{Z}/2]$. So two
exterior pairs over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with the same exponents and
non-isomorphic torsion can have isomorphic BV algebras. Over
$\mathbb{Z}$, $\Gamma=1$ and the question does not arise.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:torsioncensus}
By Corollary~\ref{thm:borel}, $(G,R)$ is exterior if and only
if $|\Gamma|$ and the torsion primes of the simple factors of
$K$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:census}) are units in $R$; over $\mathbb{Q}$
this always holds. The groups with $\Gamma\neq1$ are the
quotients of $K$ by nontrivial subgroups of its centre. For $K$
simple, with the centres from \cite[\S0.4]{Borel61},
$(G_{ss},R)$ is exterior if and only if the primes in the last
column are units in $R$:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
$G_{ss}$ & $\Gamma$ & units in $R$\\[2pt]
\hline
$\mathrm{SU}(n)/(\mathbb{Z}/d)$, $d\mid n$, $d>1$; $d=n$ is $\mathrm{PU}(n)$ & $\mathbb{Z}/d$ & primes dividing $d$\\
$\mathrm{PSp}(n)=\mathrm{Sp}(n)/(\mathbb{Z}/2)$ & $\mathbb{Z}/2$ & $2$\\
$\mathrm{SO}(n)$, $n\geq3$ & $\mathbb{Z}/2$ & $2$\\
$\mathrm{Spin}(4m{+}2)/(\mathbb{Z}/4)$ & $\mathbb{Z}/4$ & $2$\\
$\mathrm{Spin}(4m)/H$, $1\neq H\subset(\mathbb{Z}/2)^2$ & $H$ & $2$\\
$E_6/(\mathbb{Z}/3)$ & $\mathbb{Z}/3$ & $2,3$\\
$E_7/(\mathbb{Z}/2)$ & $\mathbb{Z}/2$ & $2,3$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
For $K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_s$, $\Gamma$ is any subgroup of
$\prod_iZ(K_i)$, as for $\mathrm{SO}(4)=(\mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{SU}(2))/(\mathbb{Z}/2)$.
A central quotient of $T^k\times K$ need not have torsion in
$\pi_1$: $\mathrm{U}(n)=(S^1\times\mathrm{SU}(n))/(\mathbb{Z}/n)$ has $\pi_1=\mathbb{Z}$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:hepworthSO}
Hepworth presents \cite[Theorem~4]{Hepworth}
\[
\mathbb{H}_*(L\,\mathrm{SO}(2m{+}1);\mathbb{Q})
=\mathbb{Q}[\alpha_0,\dots,\alpha_{2m-1}]/U_m\otimes
\Lambda_\mathbb{Q}[\beta_3,\dots,\beta_{4m-1}],
\qquad
\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^m\partial_i\otimes\delta_i,
\]
with $\partial_i(\alpha_j)=\alpha_{j-2i+1}$ for $j\geq2i-1$ and
$0$ otherwise. In the proof of his Proposition~18,
$\alpha_j=\omega\otimes\sigma_j$ with $\omega$ the generator of
$\pi_1=\mathbb{Z}/2$ and $\sigma_j$ Bott's generators of
$H_*(\Omega_0\mathrm{SO}(2m{+}1);\mathbb{Q})$, and $U_m$ consists of
$\omega^2=1$ and Bott's relations times $\omega^2$. Since
$\partial_i(\alpha_0)=0$, each $\partial_i$ acts on the
$\sigma_j$ alone: the BV operator is
$1\otimes\Delta_{\mathrm{Spin}(2m+1)}$, as
Theorem~\ref{thm:torsionss} predicts, and the shear of
Proposition~\ref{thm:shear} makes it the pure tensor of
$S^3\times\cdots\times S^{4m-1}$. Likewise for
$\mathrm{SO}(2m{+}2)$, the extra generator
$\varepsilon_m=1\otimes\varepsilon$ carrying no $\omega$.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
For $p\mid|\Gamma|$ the pair $(G,\mathbb{F}_p)$ is not exterior
(Remark~\ref{rem:pi1tors}): $p_*$ is not an isomorphism, and
in Lemma~\ref{lem:suspcomp} the Hurewicz image of some $g$ in
$H_1(G_{ss};\mathbb{F}_p)=\Gamma\otimes\mathbb{F}_p$ is nonzero, so the
BV operator acts on the group ring, as in Hepworth's mod~$2$
computation for $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ \cite{Hepworth}.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
